knowledge_point.title: Finding a Scalar Factor in a Linear Combination

question.:question/problem:
The arrows show $\overrightarrow{OA}=\mathbf a$, $\overrightarrow{OB}=\mathbf b$, and $\overrightarrow{OC}=\mathbf c$. Grid squares have side length one unit.

![](images/9b/9b17ef98c7d998ab367ffc7ae636fdbf978b64ed78cca5faf475f67fe2d778b6.png)

Given that $\mathbf{c}=\lambda\mathbf{a}+2\mathbf{b}$, find $\lambda$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Construct the known component $2\mathbf{b}$ from $O$, and call its endpoint $P$. Count signed horizontal and vertical grid displacements:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\overrightarrow{OP} &=2\,(-1, 2)=(-2, 4). \\
\overrightarrow{PC} &=(-6, 0).
\end{aligned}
$$

![](images/5f/5f334fa94f71ecb1afa218bb5f62110ae62e77892a75658aedc55d060bae39a1.png)

Compare the remaining displacement with $\mathbf{a}$, whose grid displacement is $(-2, 0)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Horizontal scale} &=\frac{-6}{-2}=3
\end{aligned}
$$

The scale is positive, so the remaining vector has the same direction as $\mathbf{a}$. Thus $\overrightarrow{PC}=3\mathbf{a}$. By the triangle law,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf{c} &=\overrightarrow{OP}+\overrightarrow{PC} \\
&=2\mathbf{b}+3\mathbf{a} \\
&=3\mathbf{a}+2\mathbf{b}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are not parallel, so their coefficients are unique. Matching the coefficient of $\mathbf{a}$ gives $\lambda=3$.

conversions: Reduce grid displacement ratio to a positive rational scalar

knowledge_point.title: Finding a Scalar Factor in a Linear Combination

question.:question/problem:
The arrows show $\overrightarrow{OA}=\mathbf a$, $\overrightarrow{OB}=\mathbf b$, and $\overrightarrow{OC}=\mathbf c$. Grid squares have side length one unit.

![](images/f9/f9f9267ab080572d167b3d3a52dee7bdaf8a0cbcbe7ee8b24f62bec4513975ce.png)

Given that $\mathbf{c}=\lambda\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}$, find $\lambda$.

$\lambda=$ {{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Construct the known component $\mathbf{b}$ from $O$, ending at $B$. Count signed horizontal and vertical grid displacements:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\overrightarrow{OB} &=1\,(0, -5)=(0, -5). \\
\overrightarrow{BC} &=(5, -10).
\end{aligned}
$$

![](images/23/234562f6ec422c0336bbd9f206a98ceb1cbf5b8f02dd28e57713ed82401f69ff.png)

Compare the remaining displacement with $\mathbf{a}$, whose grid displacement is $(2, -4)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Horizontal scale} &=\frac{5}{2}=\frac{5}{2} \\
\text{Vertical scale} &=\frac{-10}{-4}=\frac{5}{2}
\end{aligned}
$$

The scale is positive, so the remaining vector has the same direction as $\mathbf{a}$. Thus $\overrightarrow{BC}=\frac{5}{2}\mathbf{a}$. By the triangle law,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf{c} &=\overrightarrow{OB}+\overrightarrow{BC} \\
&=\mathbf{b}+\frac{5}{2}\mathbf{a} \\
&=\frac{5}{2}\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are not parallel, so their coefficients are unique. Matching the coefficient of $\mathbf{a}$ gives $\lambda=\frac{5}{2}$.
